message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"6014f40bd9d0c76532ffd432d2b91b4a30beb0503f0113207aec95bc8921f39f","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sc-class-d:lineage:72","source_registry_sha256":"61c32f86a25e3c021742b3c9ddf64a97709817dd75a19df6d2b69eac0a40c4f1","units":[{"unit_id":"sec09-u01","module_id":"sec09-m01","objective_ids":["sec09-u01"],"title":{"text":"Turning correctly","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Correct lane position and searching make turns predictable for everyone around you.","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F05","sec09-F06"]},{"text":"Yielding on left turns prevents collisions with oncoming traffic.","fact_ids":["sec09-F06"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Rae needs to turn left at an intersection with oncoming cars approaching.","fact_ids":["sec09-F06"]},"reasoning":{"text":"When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and always turn from the left-most part of your lane.","fact_ids":["sec09-F06","sec09-R02"]},"result":{"text":"Rae moves to the left-most part of her lane, waits for oncoming cars to pass, then turns while looking through the turn.","fact_ids":["sec09-F06","sec09-F03"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a wide swing to the left makes a right turn easier.","fact_ids":["sec09-F04"]},"correction":{"text":"On a right turn, avoid swinging wide to the left; always turn right from the right-most part of your lane.","fact_ids":["sec09-F04","sec09-F05"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Right turns hug the right, left turns hug the left and yield.","fact_ids":["sec09-F05","sec09-F06"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"From which part of your lane should a right turn begin?","fact_ids":["sec09-F05"]},"answer":{"text":"The right-most part.","fact_ids":["sec09-F05"]},"rationale":{"text":"Right turns start from the right-most part of the lane, just as left turns start from the left-most part.","fact_ids":["sec09-F05","sec09-R02"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Making safe turns","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F05","sec09-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Search and signal","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F05","sec09-F06"]},{"text":"Lane position for each turn","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F05","sec09-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Turns are among the most common maneuvers you make, and the manual sets out a clear routine for them. Before turning, search every corner for traffic controls, pedestrians and other vehicles, and signal what you intend to do. Get into and stay in the lane nearest the direction you plan to turn. During the turn, look through it to the farthest point you can see along your intended path. In this unit you will also learn which part of the lane each turn starts from, how to handle several turning lanes, and what to do once the turn is complete.","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F05","sec09-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Before and during a turn","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Search corners, signal intent","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03"]},{"text":"Use the lane nearest the turn","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03"]},{"text":"Look through to your path","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Before turning, search every corner for traffic controls, pedestrians and other vehicles, and signal what you intend to do. Get into and stay in the lane nearest the direction you plan to turn, so you are already in position when the turn begins. During a turn, look through it to the farthest point you can see along your intended path rather than at the road right in front of your hood. These three habits, searching and signaling, choosing the nearest lane, and looking through the turn, apply to right and left turns alike.","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Right turns","fact_ids":["sec09-F05","sec09-F04","sec09-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Turn from the right-most part","fact_ids":["sec09-F05","sec09-F04","sec09-F01"]},{"text":"No wide swing to the left","fact_ids":["sec09-F05","sec09-F04","sec09-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Always make a right turn from the right-most part of your lane. On a right turn, avoid swinging wide to the left before you turn. A wide swing to the left can make other drivers think you are changing lanes or turning left, and it can leave room for another vehicle to slip in beside you. Keeping to the right-most part of your lane makes your intention clear. Combine that lane position with your right signal, a search of every corner for pedestrians and vehicles, and a look through the turn to your intended path. The right-most part of the lane is where every right turn begins.","fact_ids":["sec09-F05","sec09-F04","sec09-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Left turns and multiple lanes","fact_ids":["sec09-F06","sec09-R02","sec09-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Yield to oncoming traffic","fact_ids":["sec09-F06","sec09-R02","sec09-R03"]},{"text":"Turn from the left-most part","fact_ids":["sec09-F06","sec09-R02","sec09-R03"]},{"text":"Stay in your chosen turn lane","fact_ids":["sec09-F06","sec09-R02","sec09-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic and always turn from the left-most part of your lane. Right turns start from the right-most part of your lane and left turns from the left-most part, so the side of the lane matches the direction of the turn. Where more than one lane turns, pick and enter the lane you will turn from and stay in that same lane until the turn is finished. Drifting into another turning lane partway through the turn puts you in the path of a driver turning beside you. Left turns always start from the left-most part of your lane, after yielding to oncoming traffic.","fact_ids":["sec09-F06","sec09-R02","sec09-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The wide swing trap","fact_ids":["sec09-F04","sec09-F05","sec09-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Do not swing left before a right turn","fact_ids":["sec09-F04","sec09-F05","sec09-R02"]},{"text":"Match lane side to turn direction","fact_ids":["sec09-F04","sec09-F05","sec09-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some drivers swing wide to the left before a right turn, thinking it makes the turn easier. The manual says to avoid swinging wide to the left before you turn and to always make a right turn from the right-most part of your lane. Right turns start from the right-most part of your lane and left turns from the left-most part, so the side of the lane matches the direction of the turn. Following that simple match keeps your movement predictable and keeps other vehicles from moving into the space you open up.","fact_ids":["sec09-F04","sec09-F05","sec09-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Quick turning check","fact_ids":["sec09-F05","sec09-R02","sec09-F04","sec09-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"A right turn ahead","fact_ids":["sec09-F05","sec09-R02","sec09-F04","sec09-F06"]},{"text":"Which part of the lane?","fact_ids":["sec09-F05","sec09-R02","sec09-F04","sec09-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: you are about to make a right turn. From which part of your lane should it start? The answer is the right-most part of your lane. Right turns start from the right-most part and left turns from the left-most part, so the side of the lane matches the direction of the turn. Avoid swinging wide to the left before a right turn. And for a left turn, remember the extra duty: yield to oncoming traffic before turning from the left-most part of your lane. Search every corner and signal before either kind of turn, and look through the turn to your intended path.","fact_ids":["sec09-F05","sec09-R02","sec09-F04","sec09-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Turning recap","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F04","sec09-F05","sec09-F06","sec09-R02","sec09-R03","sec09-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Search, signal, nearest lane","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F04","sec09-F05","sec09-F06","sec09-R02","sec09-R03","sec09-R01"]},{"text":"Right from the right, left from the left","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F04","sec09-F05","sec09-F06","sec09-R02","sec09-R03","sec09-R01"]},{"text":"Finish smoothly, signal off","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F04","sec09-F05","sec09-F06","sec09-R02","sec09-R03","sec09-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, before turning search every corner, signal, and get into the lane nearest your turn, then look through the turn to your intended path. Make right turns from the right-most part of your lane without swinging wide, and left turns from the left-most part after yielding to oncoming traffic. Where several lanes turn, stay in the lane you chose. Once a turn is complete, speed up smoothly to a suitable speed, check that your turn signal has switched off and keep track of traffic behind you. Where several lanes turn, stay in the one you chose until the turn is finished.","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F04","sec09-F05","sec09-F06","sec09-R02","sec09-R03","sec09-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec09-u02","module_id":"sec09-m02","objective_ids":["sec09-u02"],"title":{"text":"Turnabouts","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F09"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Turnabouts let you reverse direction when going around the block is not practical.","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-F12"]},{"text":"Each turnabout has a set order of steps, and doing them in order keeps you safe.","fact_ids":["sec09-F14","sec09-F17"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ben is on a quiet, narrow two-lane road with no U-turn room and no block to circle.","fact_ids":["sec09-F12"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A three-point turnabout fits only when the street is too narrow for a U-turn, you cannot go around the block, and the two-lane road is not busy.","fact_ids":["sec09-F12","sec09-R07"]},"result":{"text":"Ben pulls to the right edge, turns hard left across, backs hard right, then drives hard left into the right lane of the new direction.","fact_ids":["sec09-F14","sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a three-point turn may use a driveway like a two-point turnabout.","fact_ids":["sec09-R04"]},"correction":{"text":"A two-point turnabout relies on a driveway or alley, while a three-point turn must be done without using a side street or driveway at all.","fact_ids":["sec09-R04","sec09-F13"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Two-point uses a driveway; three-point uses only the road: right edge, hard left, hard right back, hard left away.","fact_ids":["sec09-R04","sec09-F14","sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"When is a three-point turnabout the right choice?","fact_ids":["sec09-F12"]},"answer":{"text":"Only when the street is too narrow for a U-turn, you cannot go around the block, and the two-lane road is not busy.","fact_ids":["sec09-F12"]},"rationale":{"text":"On a busy street, circling the block is better than a three-point turnabout.","fact_ids":["sec09-F12","sec09-R07"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Turning around","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-R04","sec09-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two-point turnabouts","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-R04","sec09-F12"]},{"text":"Three-point turnabouts","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-R04","sec09-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"Sometimes you need to reverse your direction. A two-point turnabout uses a street, alley or driveway to reverse direction when driving around a block is impractical or impossible. A three-point turnabout uses only the road itself and is allowed only in narrow conditions. In this unit you will learn the reverse two-point turnabout, the forward two-point turnabout, when a three-point turn is allowed, what it must avoid and its four steps. A two-point turnabout relies on a driveway or alley, while a three-point turn must be done without using a side street or driveway at all.","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-R04","sec09-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Reverse two-point turnabout","fact_ids":["sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Signal right, stop, check","fact_ids":["sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-R05"]},{"text":"Back to the driveway's near edge","fact_ids":["sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-R05"]},{"text":"Steer hard right, center, stop","fact_ids":["sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"For a reverse two-point turnabout, signal right, stop and check traffic to the sides and rear, then back up until your rear bumper reaches the near edge of the driveway. While backing slowly into the driveway, steer quickly all the way to the right, then straighten the wheels and stop once the vehicle is centered in the driveway. The reverse two-point turnabout ends with a shift to drive, a check both ways and, if clear, a signal and a left turn into the proper lane. Each part of the maneuver starts with a check for traffic.","fact_ids":["sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Forward two-point turnabout","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F11","sec09-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Signal left, pull in to the left","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F11","sec09-R06"]},{"text":"Stop as the rear clears the edge","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F11","sec09-R06"]},{"text":"Back out turning right","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F11","sec09-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"For a forward two-point turnabout, check your mirrors, signal left, ease toward the road's center, then pull into the alley or driveway keeping as far to its left side as you can. Stop when the rear of the vehicle clears the curb or driveway edge, check every direction, signal right and shift into reverse. The forward two-point turnabout ends by backing slowly while turning the wheel fully right, then straightening, stopping, shifting to drive, cancelling the right signal and moving forward once centered in the nearest lane.","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F11","sec09-R06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Driveway or no driveway","fact_ids":["sec09-R04","sec09-F13","sec09-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two-point: uses a driveway or alley","fact_ids":["sec09-R04","sec09-F13","sec09-F12"]},{"text":"Three-point: never uses one","fact_ids":["sec09-R04","sec09-F13","sec09-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Because both maneuvers turn you around, drivers sometimes mix their rules. A two-point turnabout relies on a driveway or alley, while a three-point turn must be done without using a side street or driveway at all. A three-point turn also must not hit the curb or leave the road surface. And it is allowed only when the street is too narrow for a U-turn, you cannot go around the block, and the two-lane road is not busy. If you need a driveway to make it work, you are doing a two-point turnabout instead.","fact_ids":["sec09-R04","sec09-F13","sec09-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Three-point steps one and two","fact_ids":["sec09-F14","sec09-F15","sec09-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Step one: signal right, stop at edge","fact_ids":["sec09-F14","sec09-F15","sec09-F13"]},{"text":"Step two: signal left, hard left across","fact_ids":["sec09-F14","sec09-F15","sec09-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Three-point step one: check the mirrors, turn on the right signal to show you are pulling to the right edge, and stop there. Three-point step two: signal left, check traffic and your left blind spot over your shoulder, then turn hard left across the road and stop when you reach the other side. So the first two steps take you from the right edge of the road to the far side, each beginning with a signal and a check. The three-point turn must still be done without hitting the curb or leaving the road surface. Signal and check traffic before each of these first two steps.","fact_ids":["sec09-F14","sec09-F15","sec09-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s6","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Three-point steps three and four","fact_ids":["sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Step three: reverse, look back, hard right","fact_ids":["sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]},{"text":"Step four: drive, hard left, straight on","fact_ids":["sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"Three-point step three: shift to reverse, check traffic and both blind spots over your shoulders instead of trusting the rearview mirror alone, then turn hard right back across and stop. Three-point step four: shift to drive, check traffic and blind spots, turn hard left into the right lane of the new direction, make sure the signal has cancelled and drive straight on. Together the four steps are: right edge and stop, hard left across, hard right back in reverse, and hard left away into the right lane of the new direction.","fact_ids":["sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Quick turnabout check","fact_ids":["sec09-F12","sec09-R07","sec09-F13","sec09-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Three-point turnabout","fact_ids":["sec09-F12","sec09-R07","sec09-F13","sec09-F07"]},{"text":"When is it allowed?","fact_ids":["sec09-F12","sec09-R07","sec09-F13","sec09-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: when is a three-point turnabout the right choice? The answer is only when the street is too narrow for a U-turn and you cannot go around the block, and only on a two-lane road that is not busy. When the street is busy, circling an entire city block is better. Remember too that a three-point turn must be done without hitting the curb, leaving the road surface or using a side street or driveway, while a two-point turnabout uses a street, alley or driveway to reverse direction. A three-point turn must also be done without hitting the curb or leaving the road surface.","fact_ids":["sec09-F12","sec09-R07","sec09-F13","sec09-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Turnabouts recap","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-R05","sec09-F10","sec09-F11","sec09-R06","sec09-R04","sec09-F12","sec09-R07","sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two-point uses a driveway or alley","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-R05","sec09-F10","sec09-F11","sec09-R06","sec09-R04","sec09-F12","sec09-R07","sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]},{"text":"Three-point only on quiet narrow roads","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-R05","sec09-F10","sec09-F11","sec09-R06","sec09-R04","sec09-F12","sec09-R07","sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]},{"text":"Right edge, hard left, hard right, hard left","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-R05","sec09-F10","sec09-F11","sec09-R06","sec09-R04","sec09-F12","sec09-R07","sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, a two-point turnabout uses a street, alley or driveway to reverse direction when driving around a block is impractical: the reverse method backs into the driveway steering hard right, and the forward method pulls in to the left and backs out turning right. first make sure your path is clear and no traffic is crossing.","fact_ids":["sec09-F22","sec09-F21"]},"result":{"text":"Lee waits for the crossing car to clear, looks left, right and left again, then enters.","fact_ids":["sec09-F21","sec09-F22"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking an approaching car's turn signal means it is safe to pull out.","fact_ids":["sec09-F23"]},"correction":{"text":"Do not turn into a lane just because an approaching vehicle is signaling, since the driver may turn after passing you or may have left the signal on.","fact_ids":["sec09-F23","sec09-R09"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Slow and scan, left-right-left, green means check, signals can mislead.","fact_ids":["sec09-F18","sec09-F21","sec09-F22","sec09-F23"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"After stopping at an intersection, in what order should you look before entering?","fact_ids":["sec09-F21"]},"answer":{"text":"Left, then right, then left again.","fact_ids":["sec09-F21"]},"rationale":{"text":"Taking extra time for crossing vehicles and bicyclists, you look left, right and left again before you enter.","fact_ids":["sec09-F21"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec09-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Safe at intersections","fact_ids":["sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F21","sec09-F22","sec09-F23"]},"lines":[{"text":"Slow down and scan","fact_ids":["sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F21","sec09-F22","sec09-F23"]},{"text":"Do not rely on others","fact_ids":["sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F21","sec09-F22","sec09-F23"]}],"narration":{"text":"Intersections are where traffic from different directions meets, so they demand extra attention. Whenever you reach an intersection, reduce speed and scan for traffic controls, cross and oncoming traffic, people walking or cycling, the state of the road and spots where you cannot see well. In this unit you will learn why you should not depend on other road users, how to look before entering, what to do when a light turns green, how big a gap you need, and why another driver's turn signal is not a reason to pull out.","fact_ids":["sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F21","sec09-F22","sec09-F23"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Scanning and expectations","fact_ids":["sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F20"]},"lines":[{"text":"Slow and scan everything","fact_ids":["sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F20"]},{"text":"Do not depend on others obeying","fact_ids":["sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F20"]},{"text":"Be ready for drivers who do not yield","fact_ids":["sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F20"]}],"narration":{"text":"Whenever you reach an intersection, reduce speed and scan for traffic controls, cross and oncoming traffic, people walking or cycling, the state of the road and spots where you cannot see well. Do not depend on other road users to obey signals or signs, because you can control only your own driving. Some road users may not yield the right-of-way, so always be prepared to avoid a collision. Scanning gives you the information, and the expectation that others may make mistakes keeps you ready to react if they do. Scanning covers traffic controls, traffic, pedestrians, cyclists, the road and blind spots.","fact_ids":["sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F20"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Before you enter","fact_ids":["sec09-F21","sec09-F22","sec09-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Extra time for crossing traffic","fact_ids":["sec09-F21","sec09-F22","sec09-R08"]},{"text":"Look left, right, left","fact_ids":["sec09-F21","sec09-F22","sec09-R08"]},{"text":"Green means check first","fact_ids":["sec09-F21","sec09-F22","sec09-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Once you have stopped at an intersection, give yourself extra time to spot crossing vehicles and bicyclists, and look left, then right, then left again before you enter. When a light turns green, do not move straight into the intersection; first make sure your path is clear and no traffic is crossing.
